title: Map What December Actually Needs to Close
teaser: Year-end pressure is easier to manage when unfinished work is sorted before it becomes urgent.
full_text: Divide December work into three groups today: must finish, intentionally carry forward, and stop. Do not treat every open item as equally deserving of a year-end deadline.

title: Shrink the Next Step of One Stalled Task
teaser: A task can feel large because its next action is still undefined.
full_text: Choose one item that has been waiting and write only the next physical action required. A concrete step is often easier to execute than a broad task label.

title: Compare One Past Decision With Its Outcome
teaser: A sensible decision and a successful result are related but not identical.
full_text: Pick one meaningful decision from this year. Put the reasoning you had then beside the outcome you can see now, and note what you read well and what you missed.

title: Clean One File Structure You Use Often
teaser: If finding a file depends on memory, the structure may be doing too little work.
full_text: Improve one frequently used folder today. Standardize names, separate old versions, or move ambiguous files into a clearer location.

title: Look at the Annual Cost of One Recurring Expense
teaser: A small monthly charge can look different when viewed as a full-year total.
full_text: Choose one recurring expense and calculate what it costs across twelve months. Compare that total with the value you actually receive before deciding whether to keep it unchanged.

title: Define the Final Check Before One Delivery
teaser: Quality improves when the last review is designed before the deadline.
full_text: For one active piece of work, write the three things that must be checked immediately before delivery. Prepare the review before the work is finished, not after a problem appears.

title: Compare One Commitment With Real Calendar Capacity
teaser: A promised date can drift away from the workload that must fit before it.
full_text: Review one upcoming delivery together with the work already on your calendar. If the timing no longer looks realistic, discuss scope or date before the final day arrives.

title: Record One Success With Evidence
teaser: Memory tends to preserve a selective version of what was actually completed.
full_text: Choose one concrete accomplishment from this year and store a short record with supporting evidence such as a result, number, document, or useful piece of feedback.

title: Remove One Unnecessary Step From a Routine
teaser: Improvement does not always require adding another control or tool.
full_text: Review one repeated routine from start to finish. Remove or combine one step that no longer contributes meaningfully to the result.

title: Define the Exit Condition for One Meeting
teaser: A discussion can expand indefinitely when nobody knows what completion should produce.
full_text: Before one important conversation today, write the decision, list, or next action that should exist by the end. Use that outcome to keep the discussion focused.

title: Put One Important Expectation in Writing
teaser: Verbal agreements can become different memories over time.
full_text: Write down one important agreement about timing, responsibility, or scope in a short neutral message. The goal is shared memory, not extra bureaucracy.

title: Evaluate a Goal With Its Costs Included
teaser: The value of a goal is not measured only by what it produced.
full_text: Choose one goal you pursued this year. List the benefit beside its cost in time, attention, and money, then decide whether the same approach still deserves another year.

title: Check That One Backup Can Actually Be Read
teaser: A backup file is useful only if it can be opened and contains what you expect.
full_text: Verify one critical backup in a controlled way today. Confirm that it is readable and includes the expected material rather than assuming its presence means recovery would work.

title: Complete the Context Before Handing Off Work
teaser: A handoff without context can force the next person to restart the investigation.
full_text: When transferring one task today, include its purpose, current state, important files, and next decision point in a short handoff note.

title: Refresh the Midmonth Closing Plan
teaser: A December plan should change when real progress makes the original version unrealistic.
full_text: Return to the closing list you made at the beginning of the month. Carry forward or stop items that clearly will not finish instead of compressing everything into the remaining days.

title: Extract One Usable Lesson From a Failed Attempt
teaser: An unsuccessful result is more useful when it points to something that can actually change.
full_text: Choose one attempt from this year that did not work as expected. Replace personal judgment with one specific process or assumption you would change next time.

title: Reduce One Permission to What Is Actually Needed
teaser: Extra access can create risk long after the original reason for granting it disappears.
full_text: Review one account, folder, or shared workspace today. Remove access that is no longer necessary while keeping the permissions required for current work.

title: Turn One Repeated Task Into a Template
teaser: Repeated work should not require rebuilding the same starting structure every time.
full_text: Choose one task you performed several times this month and create a reusable short template, checklist, or starter document. Next time, edit only what changes.

title: Choose an Early Warning Signal for One Risk
teaser: A problem is harder to manage when the first signal arrives after the damage is done.
full_text: For one upcoming responsibility, choose an early indicator such as delayed replies, rising errors, falling balance, or slipping milestones. Decide what would make you intervene.

title: Find the Repeatable Part of One Good Result
teaser: A good outcome may contain both strong process and good luck.
full_text: Review one successful piece of work from this year. Separate the practices you could deliberately repeat from the parts that depended on circumstances you did not control.

title: Set One Boundary During Year-End Pressure
teaser: Not every request that arrives late in the year deserves immediate priority.
full_text: Compare new requests with the work you have already chosen to close. If something cannot fit honestly, renegotiate timing or scope early instead of absorbing it silently.

title: Make the Last Updated Date Visible
teaser: Old information can cause bad decisions when it still looks current.
full_text: Add a visible last-updated date and, when useful, an owner to one document or list that people rely on. Give readers a way to judge how current the information is.

title: Review One Delivery From the Recipient's View
teaser: Work can be technically finished while still being difficult for someone else to use.
full_text: Open one delivery as if you were seeing it for the first time. Check whether the file name, access, explanation, and next step are clear without extra context.

title: Leave One Small Gap Unfilled
teaser: Open time does not have to become another task immediately.
full_text: If a small gap appears in your schedule today, consider protecting it for rest, reflection, or clearing minor loose ends instead of automatically filling it with new work.

title: Pass Along One Useful Thing You Learned
teaser: Useful knowledge becomes less fragile when it does not remain in one person's memory.
full_text: Choose one method, shortcut, or check that helped you this year and explain it briefly to someone who could benefit from using it.

title: Give Carried-Forward Work Its First Date
teaser: Work moved into the new year can disappear when it is assigned only to 'later.'
full_text: For each important item you deliberately carry forward, set at least the first review or start date. Give the work a visible place instead of an indefinite future label.

title: Review One Subscription Against Actual Use
teaser: Remembered use and measured use can tell different stories.
full_text: Choose one service you pay for regularly and compare the cost with your real use over the last few months. Consider cancelling, reducing, or replacing it if the value is weak.

title: List the Year's Open Loops
teaser: Unfinished matters become easier to manage when they are visible and classified.
full_text: Collect the open issues still occupying your attention. Give each one a clear decision: finish, schedule, delegate, or drop.

title: Choose One Thing to Do Less Next Year
teaser: Improvement can come from subtraction as well as addition.
full_text: Choose one behavior, meeting, expense, or distraction you want less of next year. Name what you intend to put in its place so the change has a practical direction.

title: Gather the Year's Important Records
teaser: Scattered evidence makes later review and recovery harder than necessary.
full_text: Collect important reports, receipts, results, agreements, or notes from this year into the appropriate location. Check retention needs before deleting anything.

title: Close the Year With the Real State of Things
teaser: A useful year-end review does not need to turn the year into a perfect story.
full_text: Record what finished, what remains incomplete, what you chose to stop, and what you learned. Carry forward only selected responsibilities and keep unresolved work visible.
